content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper aims to solve a sparse Nerf. Original Nerf degenerates when input views are sparse, for example, 3 views or 6 views in the paper. This paper proposes to explore the correspondences of points in different views and treat the points having correspondence with a much larger weight in re-rendering loss. To do so, the paper uses MVSnerf to initialize and computes a depth image for each input view. By checking the consistency in depth by re-projecting points from one view to another, a mask of the corresponding points is obtained. The mask is used to reweight the re-rendering loss. The idea is ok, but not easy to follow. The experiments are insufficient.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
It is cool to do nerf with only 3 views, which is very challenging. 
Codes are supplied, which are helpful for understanding. 
It is good that the method is supposed to be a portable module, and can be incorporated with any Nerf backbone. 
For the initialization problem of nerf, this paper proposes to initialize bias as an uniform distribution. 

Weakness
The paper uses MVSNerf to get depth as additional inputs, but from Fig.3 we see noises around the mask. I guess they are from the incorrect depth? Or from the inaccurate process of deriving hard-mask? I am not sure and it is not discussed in the paper. The masks are one of the contributions, but they are far from good. 
Quantitative evaluations are questionable. Improvements are minor, especially for IBRNet and MVSNerf. It is very strange that in Fig.6, IBRNet and MVSNerf are not visualized. Only one data is shown in Fig. 7 to demonstrate MVSNerf performs worse. Why not include MVSNerf and IBRNet in Fig. 6? It is very hard to get a fair comparison from limited results. 
In Table 6, the performance of mask rcnn is very close to DH-mask and H-mask. Why not compare with a baseline of Nerf + rcnn mask? 
With a lot of works on sparse Nerf, in the paper, authors did not compare with any of them. 
The performances of DH-mask and H-mask are close. 
No input views are shown, and it is hard to see how close the input views are, and how close the novel view and input views are.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Not very good in clarity and quality, novelty. 
Good in reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: Considering the unclear presentations of the paper, especially insufficient experiments. I give a reject. The paper needs a lot of polishment.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper addresses the problem of neural radiance fields from sparse views. Based on the existing NeRF methods, this paper proposes to use a mask to reweight the importance of different pixels in the training loss. The mask is constructed with geometric consistency. It highlights pixels where the correspondence of this pixel between different views can be constructed.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 

+ Highlighting the importance of pixels whose correspondences between different views can be constructed during training is reasonable. + It is a simple and effective method. 

Weakness:

- Although the proposed method is effective, the contribution and novelty are not significant enough for an ICLR paper. 
- I can understand the hard mask (H-Mask) is derived from depth data, either from a pretrained NeRF or GT depths. However, the generation method of DH-Mask is unclear. It is said the DH-Mask is extracted by "masking pixels from the largest top-K loss values at the beginning of the training stage." Why would the pixels with a larger loss likely have correspondences between different views? 


Other comments. 
The paper below also uses prior knowledge for view synthesis, although it is not a NeRF-like method. 

Shi et al. Self-supervised visibility learning for novel view synthesis, CVPR 2021.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The writing of this paper is of high quality. There are some aspects that are not clearly stated, plz refer to my comments in the question above. The novelty is insignificant. The reproducibility is good.
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed method in this paper is simple and effective. However, it is more like a small item or engineering trick in a method. The contribution is insignificant.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposed a NeRF system that gives more weight to in-mask pixels during network optimization. Specifically, the mask is computed by the left-right check in stereo matching. The author also tried to explain how this mask loss would work by transforming the mask (but does not mask sense to me).
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:

Training NeRF by giving more weight to the object of interest sounds reasonable.

Cons:

1) Definitions 3.1 and 3.2 are repeated.

2) The method is too heuristic. Equations 4, 5, 6 are just the commonly known left-right check in stereo/multi-view stereo matching, which I think are too trivial to be mentioned and could be written inline in the paragraph.

3) From my perspective, the photoconsistency could be added to the optimization in a more clever way than the hard mask proposed in the paper.  I can name several works that introduce the multi-view pixel/feature consistency during the optimization, e.g., MVSDF, NeuralWarp, GeoNeuS... The authors should investigate and compare the proposed method with the multi-view consistency in those methods.

4) I don't get the point of Proposition 1, how does it relate to the left-right check based mask?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Generally. I think the proposed method is too heuristic, and the authors should also compare with other methods which also addressed the multi-view color/feature consistencies during the optimization. Besides, some definitions/propositions in the paper do not make sense to me.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper is clearly below the bar of a top-tier conference and should be rejected.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes to regularize the optimization of NeRF based on the masks from sparse views. Hard-Mask and Degenerated Hard-Mask are proposed to assign different weights to different pixels based on the correspondence. The proposed method shows significant performance improvement on certain datasets and methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
1. This paper writes well and is very easy to understand.
2. The proposed method shows significant performance gain over the existing NeRF and IBRNet.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. I am worried about the novelty of this paper. This paper uses depth information to learn the correspondence and depth supervision has been used in the previous method as mentioned in the abstract part. Though depth has not been used to calculate the consistency, it is straightforward to use the depth to do the unprojection (image space to world space) and projection (world space to image space) operations. 
2.  As mentioned in Section 3, the Degenerated Hard-Mask is proposed based on the observation that pixels satisfying 3D correspondence tend to have a larger loss in the optimization. However, As shown in Table 1, DH-Mask shows worse or comparable results with the H-Mask. In this way, DH-Mask does not make any contribution to the proposed condition.
3. In Table 1, this papers does not show much improvement compared to IBRNet.
4. More state-of-the-arts methods of 2022 should be compared.
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed contribution is not convincing especially for the DH-Mask component.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
